title: New skill: static-verify — backend (ruff+mypy) and frontend (eslint+tsc) static analysis
description: Backend currently has no ruff or mypy configured at all — every `pr-reviewer`/`task-qa-reviewer`/`pr-decision` pass this session has reported 'no lint config exists, nothing to run' for the backend's static-analysis step. Frontend already has eslint+tsc, but there's no single reusable, directly-invokable skill for either side's static verification — it's currently done ad hoc, inline, inside pr-reviewer/task-qa-reviewer's own instructions each time. Create a new `.claude/skills/static-verify` skill that: for backend, runs ruff (lint) and mypy (type check) against `app/`; for frontend, runs `npm run lint` (eslint) and `tsc -b --noEmit`; and reports pass/fail with every finding grouped by file, distinguishing style/lint issues from real type errors. This requires first actually adding ruff+mypy as backend dev dependencies with real config, since an absent config is not something a skill can meaningfully 'run'.

checklist.step: Add `ruff` and `mypy` to `backend/pyproject.toml`'s `[project.optional-dependencies].dev`, with `[tool.ruff]` and `[tool.mypy]` config sections (reasonable defaults matching the project's existing style — e.g. line length, `target-version` 3.12; decide the mypy strictness level and record it as a `decisions` entry).

Run ruff+mypy against the existing `backend/app/` tree once added and fix any findings on already-merged code (or, per the project's non-blocking-finding rule, record any deliberately-deferred ones as a new follow-up task) — introducing a linter shouldn't ship already red.

Create `.claude/skills/static-verify/SKILL.md` (following existing skill file conventions, e.g. `architecture-review`/`check-coverage`) that runs ruff+mypy for backend and eslint+tsc for frontend, and reports results in one consistent format.
Register the new skill in CLAUDE.md's Skills list.

Decide whether `pr-reviewer.md`'s existing step 4 ('Run static analysis / linting... don't invent tool config that isn't there') and `task-qa-reviewer.md`'s equivalent step should be updated to explicitly load the new `static-verify` skill for consistency now that real config exists — record the decision either way.
Verify the skill actually catches a real issue: introduce a deliberate lint/type violation in a throwaway/test context, confirm the skill flags it, then revert — before considering this done.

decisions.decision: Backend ruff: select E (pycodestyle errors), F (pyflakes), I (isort), B (flake8-bugbear), UP (pyupgrade), SIM (flake8-simplify); ignore E501 (line-too-long); line-length=100, target-version=py312. Added `[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-bugbear].extend-immutable-calls = [fastapi.Depends, fastapi.Query, fastapi.Path, fastapi.Body, fastapi.Header, fastapi.Cookie]` so B008 doesn't flag FastAPI's own `param: X = Depends(...)` dependency-injection idiom across every route handler.
decisions.rationale: E501 is off because ~470 existing lines exceed 88 chars and 44 exceed 100, almost entirely from long, deliberately human-readable `Field(description=...)` strings in app/api/schemas.py and doc-comment-style module text that shouldn't be mechanically wrapped (see e.g. schemas.py's PositionIn.ticker description) -- ruff's own formatter can't rewrap a string literal anyway, so E501 would only ever nag, never auto-fix, on this codebase's existing style. Rejected alternative: raise line-length far enough (200+) to silence it instead of an explicit ignore -- rejected because that would also stop catching genuinely too-long *code* lines (as opposed to description strings), which a targeted E501 ignore doesn't need to trade away. B008's extend-immutable-calls addition is ruff's own documented mechanism for this exact FastAPI false-positive class (see `ruff rule B008`'s own docs) -- the alternative (per-line `# noqa: B008` on every one of the ~8 existing Depends(...) call sites, and every future one) was rejected as needless repeated noise for a pattern that's correct by FastAPI's own design, not a bug.

decisions.decision: Backend mypy strictness: a curated non-`--strict` set -- `disallow_untyped_defs`, `disallow_incomplete_defs`, `check_untyped_defs`, `no_implicit_optional`, `warn_redundant_casts`, `warn_unused_ignores`, `warn_unused_configs`, plus `ignore_missing_imports = true` -- rather than mypy's full `--strict` (which additionally turns on `disallow_any_generics`, `disallow_subclassing_any`, `warn_return_any`, `strict_equality`, and several others).
decisions.rationale: Full `--strict` would immediately fight pandas (no first-party type stubs; every DataFrame/Series operation would need explicit `Any`-suppression) and SQLAlchemy's declarative ORM patterns used in app/db/models.py, producing noise unrelated to real bugs on day one of adopting the tool -- the same 'don't ship already red, but don't make the bar so onerous nobody keeps it green' tradeoff the frontend already made for eslint (typescript-eslint's plain `recommended` config, not `recommended-type-checked`/`strict-type-checked`, per frontend/eslint.config.js). The chosen subset still catches real bugs: it's what actually caught the 4 genuine mypy findings in app/api/routers/stocks.py (AnalysisResponse being constructed with types looser than its Pydantic schema declared) during this task, which were then fixed by tightening app/signals/engine.py's SignalResult.signal/confidence_band to Literal types and adding an explicit `typing.cast` at the API boundary for screens/indicators (with a comment explaining the domain layer intentionally doesn't import API schema types, per docs/Architecture.md's layering, even though Pydantic validates the actual shape at construction time regardless). `disallow_untyped_defs` was kept on (rather than left off, which --strict does turn on but which is also independently valuable) because it's the single check most likely to catch someone accidentally skipping type annotations on a new function -- cheap to satisfy on all-new code, unlike the pandas/SQLAlchemy-hostile strict-mode checks.

decisions.decision: Updated both `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md` (step 4) and `.claude/agents/task-qa-reviewer.md` (step 3) to explicitly load and run the new `static-verify` skill, replacing their prior 'check pyproject.toml for whatever's configured, don't invent tool config that isn't there' language.
decisions.rationale: That inline language existed specifically because there was no backend lint/type config to run -- every prior pr-reviewer/task-qa-reviewer pass this session had to fall back to 'nothing to run' for the backend half of static analysis, which is precisely the gap this task exists to close. Now that real, reusable config plus a dedicated skill exist, leaving the agents' own inline ad hoc instructions in place would mean the new skill and the two agents' actual behavior silently drift apart over time (e.g. if static-verify's commands or scope change later, both agent files would need a separate, easy-to-forget update) -- pointing them at the skill keeps one source of truth, matching how they already load `code-review`/`verify-elder-signal`/`architecture-review` by reference rather than re-describing those skills' steps inline. Considered leaving the agents unchanged and only relying on someone thinking to invoke static-verify manually -- rejected because that's exactly the ad hoc, easy-to-skip pattern the task description calls out as the problem.

review.notes: Full review: backend pytest+coverage (493 passed, 99.84%), frontend vitest+coverage (99.71% stmts, unchanged by this PR, re-run for completeness, no regression), static-verify skill itself run against its own PR (ruff clean, mypy clean on 37 files, eslint clean, tsc clean), code-review skill (medium effort) returned 0 findings after an independent full-diff pass. Manually verified the Literal-type tightening on SignalResult.signal/.confidence_band is behavior-preserving: _determine_signal and confidence_band's full bodies only ever return the declared literals. Verified the cast(Screens, ...)/cast(Indicators, ...) at the stocks.py API boundary is a static-typing-only annotation -- analyse()'s screens/indicators dict literals are keyed exactly to the Screens/Indicators Pydantic schema fields, and AnalysisResponse's Pydantic construction still validates the real runtime shape regardless of the cast; consistent with docs/architecture/Backend.md's layering (domain layer doesn't import API schema types) and this task's own decisions entry. Re-ran scripts/export_openapi.py -- no diff against the committed backend/openapi.json, correct since no route signature/response_model changed. All three 'decide X' checklist items have corresponding decisions entries with rationale and rejected alternatives. No frontend/UI surface touched by this PR (backend dev tooling + agent skill/instruction files only) -- browser walkthrough explicitly skipped as not applicable. This PR updates pr-reviewer.md itself (step 4, pointing static-analysis at the new static-verify skill); reviewed under the updated instructions per CLAUDE.md's note on checked-out-branch instructions taking effect immediately, which is what surfaced the clean ruff/mypy run. No blocking or non-blocking findings; no follow-up task filed.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend pytest+coverage myself: 493 passed, 99.84% coverage, matching review notes exactly. Independently ran ruff check app/ and mypy app/ myself (not just trusting the review): both clean, mypy on 37 source files. Skimmed the full diff (git diff origin/main...HEAD): all non-typing changes are mechanical (import sort, ternary-ifs via ruff SIM). Independently traced the Literal-type tightening and cast() calls myself rather than trusting the review's claim: read _determine_signal's and confidence_band's full bodies and confirmed each only ever returns its declared literal set, and confirmed analyse()'s screens/indicators dict literals (engine.py) are keyed exactly to the Screens/Indicators Pydantic schema fields (schemas.py) that cast(Screens, ...)/cast(Indicators, ...) target in stocks.py, so the boundary cast is static-typing-only and Pydantic still validates runtime shape at AnalysisResponse construction. No frontend files touched by this PR, consistent with the review's claim. No PR comments (human or otherwise) present that would override the accept.
